# Christos Kalyvas-Kasopatidis

> Christos Kalyvas-Kasopatidis, PhD, is an AI security researcher working on the security of AI and LLM systems (AI security controls and governance, shadow-AI detection, prompt-injection testing and guardrail evaluation, agentic AI threat modelling), AI for cyber defence and vulnerability intelligence. His research background is in machine learning and multi-objective (skyline / Pareto) optimisation over big data (PhD, University of the Aegean).

This site has two parts: a blog at the root and an academic profile under /profile/.

## Profile

- [Profile and bio](https://christoskalyvas.eu/profile/): biography, research interests, education
- [Experience](https://christoskalyvas.eu/profile/experience/): positions, skills, certifications
- [Publications](https://christoskalyvas.eu/profile/publication/): journal articles, conference papers and preprints with DOIs

## Sections

- [Posts](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/): all posts, organised as /posts/<primary topic>/<post>/
- [AI Security](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/ai-security/): AI and LLM security, agentic AI, multi-agent systems
- [Security](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/security/): security outside AI (OSINT, digital identity)
- [Decision Intelligence](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/decision-intelligence/): multi-objective decisions, skylines
- [Vulnerability Intelligence](https://christoskalyvas.eu/vulnerability-intelligence/): discovery, cataloguing, prioritisation and exploitation of vulnerabilities
- [Off Duty](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/off-duty/): non-research writing, including [Life](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/off-duty/life/) and [Nautical](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/off-duty/nautical/) (sailing, navigation, seamanship)

## Blog posts

- [Hidden in an emoji: invisible instructions and language models](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/ai-security/hidden-in-an-emoji/): An emoji can carry invisible Unicode characters that a person never sees but a language model reads. How the hiding works, where prompt injection enters, and …

- [From predicting words to modelling worlds: four ideas, one city](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/ai-security/from-words-to-world-models/): Predicting the next word, reasoning, and two kinds of world model: four ideas behind today&rsquo;s AI models, explained with one taxi ride through Kavala, and …

- [Χριστούγεννα με παιδιά στη Βόρεια Ελλάδα: τρία χωριά του Άη Βασίλη](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/off-duty/life/christmas-kids-north-greece/): Ονειρούπολη Δράμας, Μύλος των Ξωτικών και Παραμυθοχώρα στο Πόζαρ: ημερομηνίες 2026–27, κριτικές και πρακτικά για γονείς, σε ένα σύνορο επιλογών.

- [Indexes and AI assistants: where retrieval meets security](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/ai-security/indexes-and-ai-assistants/): An AI assistant reads only the pages its index hands over. How vectors and embeddings choose those pages, why that helps, and why the index is also one place …

- [The swarm breach](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/ai-security/the-swarm-breach/): About 1,200 OpenAI evaluation agents coordinated through an improvised message board, and about 700 of them took part in breaching Hugging Face. The techniques …

- [I OSINT'd myself](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/security/i-osinted-myself/): A ten-minute open-source intelligence assessment of my own public footprint. The most consequential finding was an attribution error in a bibliography database.

- [What multi-objective optimisation taught me about decisions](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/decision-intelligence/multi-objective-optimisation-decisions/): Before ranking options, remove the ones that another option beats on every criterion. A lesson about decisions from a PhD on skyline queries.

- [Phronesis for agents](https://christoskalyvas.eu/posts/ai-security/phronesis-for-agents/): Rules cover the cases their authors anticipated; Aristotle&rsquo;s practical wisdom covers the rest. What this distinction means for the design of AI agents.
